title: Finite uniform scalar-perfect models on a pro-etale refinement
statement:
Let $S$ be a nonempty quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], with small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings on that site, and $\underline R\to B$ a ring-sheaf map, where underlines denote constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $P\in D(B)$ and a pro-étale covering $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ are given, together with bounded cochain complexes $F_i^\bullet$ of finite projective $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] and isomorphisms $P|_{U_i}\simeq B|_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{F_i^\bullet}$, with termwise sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Finite projective here means a direct summand of a finite free module, with splitting data as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package].

There exist a finite nonempty set $J$, a function $\alpha:J\to I$, affine opens $V_j\subset U_{\alpha(j)}$ whose composites $V_j\to S$ form a pro-étale covering, and integers $a_j\le b_j$ with $F_{\alpha(j)}^r=0$ for $r\notin[a_j,b_j]$. For $a=\min_{j\in J}a_j$ and $b=\max_{j\in J}b_j$, one has $a\le b$ and $[a_j,b_j]\subseteq[a,b]$. Put $B_j=B|_{V_j}$ and $E_j^\bullet=B_j\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{F_{\alpha(j)}^\bullet}$. Then $P|_{V_j}\simeq E_j^\bullet$, $E_j^r=0$ outside $[a_j,b_j]$, and every degree has a strict-perfect coefficient package
$$E_j^r\xrightarrow{I_{jr}}B_j^{\oplus N_{jr}}\xrightarrow{P_{jr}}E_j^r,\qquad P_{jr}I_{jr}=1,$$
where $I_{jr},P_{jr}$ are the constant-sheaf scalar extensions of a chosen splitting of $F_{\alpha(j)}^r$. These conclusions require no flatness or exactness of $B\otimes_{\underline R}-$; the integers and packages are chosen independently of any later test module sheaf.

proof.text: Apply the finite affine cover lemma to the quasi-compact open $S\subset S$, obtaining a finite affine open cover $\{A_k\}_{k\in K}$. For each $k$, apply the covering condition to the original family over $A_k$. Its affine-target refinement clause supplies a finite affine covering $\{V_{kt}\to A_k\}_{t\in J_k}$, with each $V_{kt}$ an affine open of some $U_{\alpha(k,t)}\times_S A_k$. This fibre product is the inverse image of the open $A_k$, so $V_{kt}$ is also an affine open in $U_{\alpha(k,t)}$. Use the finite affine refinement asserted in the site node, not merely joint surjectivity of an arbitrary family.

source.place: Definition 0989 (definition-fpqc-covering), applied on the finite affine open cover; the finite affine refinement clause recorded in sk-def-pe-site.

proof.text: The family $\{A_k\to S\}$ is a Zariski cover and hence a pro-étale cover by the site node. Both this family and each $\{V_{kt}\to A_k\}$ are fpqc. Composition of fpqc covering families makes $\{V_{kt}\to S\}_{(k,t)}$ fpqc. Each composite is weakly étale by stability under composition, hence this is a pro-étale cover by its definition. Set $J=\coprod_{k\in K}J_k$ and retain the indicated function $\alpha:J\to I$. A finite union of finite sets is finite. The images of these charts cover $S$; since $S$ is nonempty, $J$ is nonempty. This argument uses neither quasi-separatedness of $S$ nor quasi-compactness of the original $U_i$.

source.place: Lemma 098C (lemma-proetale), composition; its fpqc and weakly-etale components are the cited covering-axiom and stability nodes.

proof.text: For each $j$, boundedness of the given complex $F_{\alpha(j)}^\bullet$ supplies an ordered interval $[a_j,b_j]$ outside which its terms vanish. If that complex is zero, choose $a_j=b_j=0$. Since $J$ is finite and nonempty, define $a=\min_j a_j$ and $b=\max_j b_j$. For every $j$ one has $a\le a_j\le b_j\le b$; choosing any $j\in J$ also gives $a\le b$. Thus $[a_j,b_j]\subseteq[a,b]$. These choices use only the fixed complexes.

source.place: Finite minimum and maximum applied to the bounded models in the hypothesis (elementary extraction after the covering refinement).

proof.text:
Use slice sites for restriction. For $V_j\to U_{\alpha(j)}$, successive restriction is sectionwise the identity on a test object over $V_j$. The slice forgetful functor preserves covers, and a cover of its underlying test object lifts uniquely to a cover over the slice object, so it is continuous and cocontinuous. Apply the restriction/sheafification comparison to the constant module presheaves, whose restrictions are the same constant presheaves. It identifies $(\underline{F_{\alpha(j)}^r})|_{V_j}$ with $\underline{F_{\alpha(j)}^r}$ on the smaller slice, naturally in all linear maps and differentials. Apply the natural tensor restriction comparison over the constant ring sheaf $\underline R$, with $B$ regarded as an $\underline R$-module, to identify
$$(B|_{U_{\alpha(j)}}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{F_{\alpha(j)}^\bullet})|_{V_j}\cong B_j\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{F_{\alpha(j)}^\bullet}=E_j^\bullet.$$
The maps commute with differentials by the naturality in the cited comparisons.

source.place: Section 03DH (section-localize), Definition 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site); restriction/sheafification and tensor comparisons.

proof.text: Module restriction to a slice is exact by the module restriction/extension-by-zero lemma. Therefore its derived functor is represented by termwise restriction, as specified in the derived-restriction definition. Restrict the given representing isomorphism for $P|_{U_{\alpha(j)}}$, and use relocalization and the comparison of step 4. This gives $P|_{V_j}\simeq E_j^\bullet$. If $r\notin[a_j,b_j]$, the term is $B_j\otimes_{\underline R}\underline 0=0$: every generator $b\otimes0$ is zero. Thus $E_j^r=0$ outside the same interval; no preservation of a nonsplit exact sequence is involved.

source.place: Section 03DH (section-localize), Definition 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site), and ordinary sheaf tensor definition.

proof.text: For $N\ge0$, identify $B_j\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{R^{\oplus N}}$ with $B_j^{\oplus N}$ as follows. The tensor/sheafification lemma, applied to the constant ring presheaf $R$, identifies its left side with the sheafification of $W\mapsto B_j(W)\otimes_R R^{\oplus N}$. Sectionwise the map $b\otimes(r_t)_t\mapsto(br_t)_t$ has inverse $(b_t)_t\mapsto\sum_t b_t\otimes e_t$. These formulas respect restrictions, so they identify this presheaf with the already-sheaf $B_j^{\oplus N}$. They also apply for $N=0$, with the empty sum. No flatness hypothesis occurs in these inverse formulas.

source.place: Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), final sheaf-factor specialization and elementary finite-basis tensor calculation.

proof.text: Choose the degreewise splitting $F_{\alpha(j)}^r\xrightarrow{i_{jr}}R^{\oplus N_{jr}}\xrightarrow{p_{jr}}F_{\alpha(j)}^r$ in the finite-projective hypothesis. Apply constant sheafification and then $B_j\otimes_{\underline R}-$, and use step 6 on the middle term. The resulting maps $I_{jr},P_{jr}$ satisfy $P_{jr}I_{jr}(b\otimes v)=b\otimes p_{jr}i_{jr}(v)=b\otimes v$. This is an equality of presheaf tensor maps and hence of their sheafifications. They therefore give exactly the strict-perfect coefficient package of the definition. Only finitely many nonzero degrees of finitely many selected complexes require choices; outside their intervals take $N_{jr}=0$ and the zero splitting. All intervals, ranks and maps have now been chosen from the cover, the models and their splittings, before introducing any test module sheaf. The entire construction uses functoriality and split identities, so requires no flatness or exactness of scalar extension.

source.place: Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor) and the degreewise splitting convention of def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package; elementary application of the two functors to a split identity.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q27-18bf421c6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and its 7 new proof steps in full, along with every cited statement. The statement is unchanged, adds no hypothesis and is not weakened. It gives exactly what the parent lem-sfb-internal-hom-dual-tor-amplitude takes in its step 2. There are no new nodes. Step 1 uses the finite affine cover (lem-pqf) of the quasi-compact S and the covering condition of Stacks 0989 over each affine A_k, so V_kt is affine open in U_alpha. Over the affine A_k a finite affine refinement is a cover, which is true because A_k is separated. Step 2 composes covers with lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms (2), which is Stacks 022D/098C(2), and gets weak etaleness from open immersion, base change and composition. It never assumes S is quasi-separated, so there is no E1 fault, and J is nonempty because S is. Step 3 is elementary; I checked the zero-complex and disjoint-interval cases. Steps 4-5 restrict to slices via the slice sheafification and tensor comparisons; the slice forgetful functor is continuous and cocontinuous by def-pur-localized-ringed-site. They also use relocalization and exact module restriction (unit sk-def-sf-operations, which is in route), and B tensor 0 = 0. Step 6 is the final clause of Stacks 0GMW, B_j(W) tensor R^N = B_j(W)^N, including N=0. Step 7 applies a functor to p i = id, which matches the degreewise package definition. No flatness is needed (checked R=Z, B=Z/2). I searched the DAG for duplicates; the nearest are the scalar-perfect dual realization, coefficient finite-descent sections and lisse finite models nodes, and none states this. The tool_uses are generic site tools and are accepted. There are no SGA citations. No fixes were made.
